task: Add explicit, signed platform tenant selection so a platform operator can enter one webshop admin context without storefront login or first-tenant fallback.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This transaction changes canonical tenant resolution for privileged platform actors. The selected tenant must be explicit, actor-bound, signed, server-validated and fail closed without weakening customer/store RBAC or pilot acceptance.

acceptanceCriteria: A platform operator can explicitly select a pilot or active webshop from platform administration and enter /admin in that exact tenant context without storefront/customer login.
The selected context is represented by a short-lived signed HttpOnly cookie whose token is bound to both the authenticated platform actor and the exact instance id.
getCurrentWebshopInstance resolves the signed platform selection only after authenticated actor validation and current platform_operators authority, and queries only the exact selected instance.
A valid explicit selection never falls through to a different tenant if the selected instance becomes unavailable; it fails closed to null.
A different authenticated user cannot inherit another platform actor's selected context.
The platform actor can clear the explicit tenant context and return to the tenant-independent platform control center.
Pilot acceptance, merchant RBAC, customer auth, middleware and parked AAL2 enforcement remain unchanged.
invariants: DOMAIN-TENANCY owns tenant selection; identity only proves actor/platform authority.
No first-tenant, first-membership or ambiguous multi-tenant fallback is introduced.
The platform context token is cryptographically distinct from the storefront pilot acceptance token and is never used as storefront acceptance authority.
Cookie selection cannot itself grant platform authority; current platform_operators state is revalidated on resolution.
Configured tenant deployments remain authoritative before platform context resolution.
Normal merchant resolution through role_bindings remains unchanged when no actor-bound platform context exists.

failureModes: A raw instanceId cookie lets the browser choose tenant truth without server proof.
A signed token that contains only instanceId can leak context across subsequent authenticated users on the same browser.
A stale/invalid selected tenant falls through to another membership and silently changes operating scope.
The new admin context accidentally replaces or broadens Preview pilot storefront acceptance.
edgeCases: Platform actor with zero tenant memberships can select an active webshop because platform authority plus explicit target is sufficient.
Platform actor with multiple tenant bindings resolves only the selected instance.
Expired or tampered token is ignored and existing neutral/membership resolution applies.
Valid actor-bound token for an archived/suspended target resolves null rather than another tenant.
Clearing the context removes only the platform tenant cookie and returns to /admin/platform.

alternatives.summary: Reuse shoperation_pilot_acceptance as the platform admin tenant selector.
alternatives.reason: Pilot acceptance is Preview/storefront access authority with different semantics and must not become normal admin tenant context.

alternatives.summary: Add a dedicated actor-bound signed context under src/lib/instances and consume it in canonical instance resolution.
alternatives.reason: This preserves DOMAIN-TENANCY ownership, requires explicit target selection, and composes with existing platform identity without introducing a second tenant resolver.

specialistReviews.finding: Tenant selection must live under the existing instance/context authority rather than an admin-page-local resolver.
specialistReviews.resolution: Create the signed context primitive under src/lib/instances and make admin forms call it through a thin server action.

specialistReviews.finding: A signed instance-only cookie remains reusable across users and a stale selected tenant can cause scope confusion.
specialistReviews.resolution: Bind the token to actor UUID plus instance UUID and expiry; revalidate current platform role and return null directly when an explicit selected target is unavailable.

challenge.scenario: Actor A selects tenant X, logs out, Actor B signs in on the same browser.
challenge.finding: An instance-only token could leak X into Actor B's session.
challenge.resolution: Token payload includes actorId and resolution requires an exact actor match.

challenge.scenario: Selected tenant X is archived or suspended after selection.
challenge.finding: Falling back to another candidate would silently mutate operating context.
challenge.resolution: A valid explicit selection causes exact lookup and returns null if X is no longer eligible.

challenge.scenario: Merchant/non-platform actor has or forges a syntactically valid selection token.
challenge.finding: Tenant cookie must never grant cross-tenant authority.
challenge.resolution: Canonical resolver requires current platform_operators authority before honoring the token.

proofPlan: Add deterministic source-level regression proof for actor-bound signing, expiry/tamper rejection, exact selected-instance resolution, platform revalidation and no fallback.
Prove both platform control-center and webshop-management surfaces expose explicit selection while the admin shell exposes a clear-context return path.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Run Incremental Known Failure Replay and existing Control Plane sync/truth gates.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED and lifecycle closure before declaring the block complete.

requirements.requirement: Platform authority can explicitly select and clear an actor-bound signed webshop admin context, and canonical tenant resolution honors only that exact validated target without storefront login or ambiguous fallback.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A selected platform tenant context cannot be reused by a different authenticated actor.
An explicit selected tenant that cannot be resolved must not silently fall through to a different tenant.
Storefront pilot acceptance remains a separate authority and is not repurposed as normal admin tenant selection.

notes: Independent MR1 tenant-selection release unit started from main 4f6a638. PR #858 remains parked and read-only. This block does not change MFA/AAL2 policy.
